result.summary: Adds an `interfaces::Block` IPC handle and refactors `BlockTemplate` so `submitSolution()` applies solutions to a copy of the block rather than modifying the template in place. Migrates block retrieval methods (`header()`, `data()`, and `coinbaseMerklePath()`) to the new `Block` interface and changes `submitBlock()` and `submitSolution()` to return a `Block` handle alongside acceptance status. Adds functional tests exercising concurrent template reads and solution submissions.
result.problem: Concurrent IPC calls across worker threads can race on `CBlockTemplate` members when `submitSolution()` mutates the template's block in place while another thread reads from it via template getters (issue #36515). Additionally, external IPC callers could not inspect or retain rejected blocks submitted through the interface.
evidence: Author PR description: 'submitSolution() no longer modifies the template. It applies the solution to a copy of the template block and returns a Block handle for that copy, also when the block is rejected.'
result.scope_notes: Introduces breaking IPC interface changes in `mining.capnp` (assigning new Cap'n Proto method ordinals and throwing deprecation errors on old ones).
result.changed_since_previous: Replaced the previous mutex-locking and `getTotalFees()` approach with an immutable template design using an `interfaces::Block` handle. `submitSolution()` now operates on a copy of the template block rather than mutating the template under a lock.
result.card: Adds an interfaces::Block handle and refactors the mining IPC interface so submitSolution operates on a copy instead of modifying the template in place, fixing a concurrent data race between solution submission and template reads (issue #36515). Block retrieval methods are migrated to the Block interface, and submission methods now return a Block handle even when blocks are rejected. This is a breaking change for IPC mining clients (e.g. sv2-tp) using the Cap'n Proto interface.

risk.why: Modifies the mining IPC interface and Cap'n Proto schemas with breaking changes; bugs could disrupt external mining callers or pool daemons using multiprocess Bitcoin Core.
